title-group.article-title: Targeted EGFR inhibition in colorectal cancer

abstract.p: Background: Targeted inhibition of EGFR may improve outcomes for patients with advanced colorectal cancer. We assessed osimertinib in routine clinical practice. Methods: We reviewed 142 adults treated at 6 centers between 2021 and 2025. The primary endpoint was objective response, with survival and toxicity as secondary endpoints. Results: Objective response occurred in 48% of patients after a median follow-up of 18 months. Grade 3 toxicity occurred in 12% of patients. Conclusions: EGFR-directed treatment showed meaningful activity with manageable toxicity. Prospective validation is warranted.
